headline: Brent tops $90 on a ninth night of US-Iran strikes — KSE-100 sheds almost 2,000 points at the open, then claws back to close flat at 175,927.73.
summary: Brent crude broke above $90/bbl over the weekend, its highest since June, as US strikes on Iran ran a ninth straight night and Kuwait reported a hit on its own oil facility. That knocked the KSE-100 down nearly 2,000 points at Monday's open before value-buyers clawed it back to a flat +125-point close. The story cuts two ways: pricier crude is a fundamental tailwind for E&P and refining names, but a heavier import bill hits OMCs, cement, autos and exporters just as SBP reserves have slipped to $17.2bn and the government is weighing a return to austerity/fuel-saving measures. The desk stays cautious, favouring quality cash-generative names over anything geared to imports.

sectors.name: E&P (OGDC / PPL / MARI)
sectors.why: Brent above $90 lifts realized crude prices directly, and macro's own sector tilt names E&P a favourite — though all three are still trading below their 20/50-day averages on risk-off outflows, so the fundamental tailwind hasn't shown up in price yet.

sectors.name: Refineries (ATRL / NRL / PRL)
sectors.why: Higher crude plus the government's July 13 fast-track on the $6bn Brownfield Refining Policy upgrade package is a real tailwind; ATRL is the one name actually showing it today, +4.1% on 3.4x average volume.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Macro's regime read keeps banks favoured on high-rate carry and defensive quality, with T-bill cutoffs still sub-policy-rate — a quieter place to sit out an oil-driven risk-off tape.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand defensive with low direct oil-import beta, per the macro sector tilt — insulated from the crude/FX squeeze hitting importers.

sectors.name: OMCs (PSO)
sectors.why: A wider import bill and slipping forex reserves ($17.2bn, -6.7% WoW) squeeze an already thin-margin business carrying circular-debt risk; PSO's fundamentals screen only 'mixed' with a 1.4% net margin.

sectors.name: Cement / Autos
sectors.why: Both are energy-cost or imported-input sensitive, and macro explicitly flags them avoid while the oil shock and current-account deficit run together.

sectors.name: Textiles / exporters
sectors.why: June's export slowdown plus Hormuz-linked shipping and freight-cost risk stack on top of a current account that swung to a $649m deficit in June.

watchlist.angle: The one oil-linked name actually moving on this news: +4.1% today on 3.4x average volume, now trading above both its 20- and 50-day averages near a fresh high (RSI 63.6). Fundamentals screen cheap (P/E 4.49, in the bottom third of PSX), and it sits directly in the path of the government's July 13 refinery-upgrade fast-track plus results due August 11.
watchlist.risk: Thin net margin (7%) and no real dividend cushion (0.56% yield) — if crude or the naphtha/product spread reverses, there's little buffer.

watchlist.angle: Today's strongest proven-strategy trigger on the desk: 'Volume leads price' (OBV divergence) fired with a 97% historical hit rate over 89 trades, still 83% out-of-sample. Fundamentals back it up — 'attractive' rating, cheap P/E 6.62, 32% net margin, no dividend drag.
watchlist.risk: Small/mid-cap bank (Rs61bn cap) with thinner liquidity than the majors — a risk-off tape can widen slippage on both entry and exit.

watchlist.angle: The steadiest-looking E&P name today: only +0.45% but holding near its 20-day high (2.45% away) with low volatility, unlike MARI/OGDC/PPL which are all down and below their moving averages. Fundamentals rate 'attractive' — cheap P/E 7.1, 48% net margin, an 11% covered dividend — a direct crude-price beneficiary that's actually held up.
watchlist.risk: No live technical trigger yet — this is a fundamentals-plus-macro case, not a proven backtest signal, so timing entry is the open question.

watchlist.angle: The most beaten-down of the E&P names — down 11.6% over 20 sessions, RSI at 35.8 (oversold territory), 14.8% off its 20-day high — despite 'mixed' fundamentals that include a strong 34% net margin and a moderate covered dividend (3.41% yield, 26% payout). A name to watch for a mean-reversion setup if Brent holds these levels.
watchlist.risk: No trigger has actually fired yet; catching an oversold E&P name in a risk-off regime can mean catching a falling knife if the sell-off in banks/E&P continues.

catalysts.event: SBP MPC — first monetary policy decision of FY27, held at 11.5% last time citing inflation and US-Iran war uncertainty
PBS July CPI release — first print to capture this month's fuel-price hikes and the Hormuz oil spike
ATRL, NRL, POL and HBL results

risks: Further escalation on the Strait of Hormuz (a ninth straight night of strikes already, plus a hit on a Kuwaiti oil facility) could push Brent higher still and reopen the ~2,000-point intraday air-pocket seen at Monday's open.

SBP reserves have already dropped to $17.2bn (-6.7% WoW on debt repayments) and the government is weighing a return to March's austerity/fuel-conservation measures — a real, not hypothetical, forex-stress signal.
June's current account swung to a $649m deficit (from a $500m May surplus), reversing FY25's surplus trend; a sustained oil shock widens the import bill exactly where this vulnerability already sits.
